_about: Hero vehicle parameters. hue_ranges are HSV [lo,hi] pairs of the PAINT; attach_dark_max_v/_s attach the car's dark part to it (0 = the paint covers the whole car, which is the case for a car painted at both ends). open_kernel removes specks; close_kernel joins the body's halves; min_area rejects smaller things. Re-record the front/rear template afterwards and CHECK corr(right,left) is negative.
_measured: 2026-10-17, yellow nose + black cabin, 800x600. THE PAINT (the nose) is all a colour mask can see: H 24..33, S 93..138, V 115..211, stable 460..500 px, position jitter +-0.14 px. The cabin cannot be added reliably: (1) brightness - the cabin reads V 98 on one frame and 147 on another while the road beside it reads 150 and 183, so the mask flipped between whole car and nose six times in fourteen frames; (2) OUTLINE - both halves are ~36 grey levels from the road and the car's silhouette is a real closed curve, but the cabin is fragmented by its own specular reflections, so the pocket the outline seals off contains the nose plus 2.1x its area - not the car. That partial mask also flickers (1.0x..2.1x), so it is off: a stable nose with no heading beats a wandering almost-car. attach_to_outline stays in the code, off, for a car whose dark half is one clean piece. TO GET THE WHOLE CAR: paint the rear as well, so the colour mask covers both ends - which is exactly why the previous red car worked, being painted at both ends.
